correctness.rationale: The unique representatives of all unordered balanced partitions are the C(19,9)=92,378 ten-subsets containing vertex zero. Two independent exhaustive boundary computations give the full ten-value histogram and ten cost-six minima. Distance-two ball enumeration proves their exact classification and antipodal pairing. Full enumeration of 340 states and all single swaps yields exactly 2,520 edges; independent symmetric-difference checks verify every adjacency; BFS from every state establishes radius 5, diameter 6, and eccentricity counts. Pairwise common-neighbor counts and an explicit ten-label disjointness certificate establish the Petersen optimum bridge graph. The included verifier was executed successfully from its actual artifact path; the finite enumeration has bounded exact integer operations.

value.rationale: The first-excitation budget is canonically forced by the parity of boundary sizes in a cubic 20-vertex balanced graph, so the cutoff is mathematically intrinsic rather than arbitrarily selected. Characterization of the ten minimum bisections and their previously inaccessible transitions tests a central practical question in constrained partition optimization: how much objective degradation is necessary and sufficient to move between global minimizers? The sharp slack-two answer, connected 340-state component, exact metric, and Petersen-shaped optimum-bridge structure offer a natural complete small-instance benchmark. The problem has an inherent object/invariant motivation, even though it is finite and makes no asymptotic claim.
